messages.subject: [D-RUG] Open work session this week and functions workshop next week
messages.subject_clean: [D-RUG] Open work session this week and functions workshop next week
messages.body_plain:
Hi D-RUGgies!

We will be meeting this Thursday (1/30) from 10-noon virtually and in person in the DataLab classroom (Library 360). This is a group working session so come with your questions for our expeRts, or just bring your laptop and get in some distraction free R-coding time. Additionally, if there are topics you would like to see someone do a deeper dive on, let us know!

In addition, next week we will be having a workshop on how to write your own functions! If this sounds scary, don't worry. There will be step by step instructions and live coding to walk you through the process! If you have ever lamented having to make the same change or correction many places in your code or if you find yourself copy/paste/modifying your code a lot, this workshop will be super helpful! Even if you don't do these things, functions can be a great way to organize your code and take your reproducibility skills to the next level.

Datalab will also be open for Tea Time and Co-working on Thursday afternoon.

D-RUG: 10am-noon, DataLab Classroom, Library 360, and zoom https://ucdavis.zoom.us/j/96397082218?pwd=S0JXcW5hcUFkbTcwMHFQV1NVNkg3Zz09
Tea Time: 1-2pm, DataLab Classroom, Library 360
Co-working: 2-4pm, DataLab Classroom Room, Library 360

Please consider posting your questions to our Discourse <https://d-rug.discourse.group/> site in advance of attending D-RUG virtually. This helps us do a better job of answering your questions, and also keep a log of the types of questions we see frequently.

See you then,

Your D-RUG Coo[R]dinators

messages.subject: [D-RUG] Custom Functions Workshop Source Material
messages.body_plain:
Hi D-RUGies!

Tomorrow's function writing workshop will be based on this git repository: https://github.com/d-rug/2025_writing_functions. Feel free to poke around and download/clone it early so you can follow along on your own computer. You can also follow the same steps using your own code if you would prefer that. There will be plenty of time for troubleshooting if you get stuck.

See you tomorrow,

Your D-RUG Coo[R]dinators
